task.heading: The task
paragraphs: **River Portal**: a charity portal where needs meet gifts, carried by coordinators and carriers. Privacy is strict, a gift is a gift, and every public number comes from an append-only log.
Delivered in iterations 00–04: a 146-note specification, 23 ADRs, 17 packages behind gates, a public site and a studio, a Pulumi program, 9 demo personas and 3 organisation profiles.

observations.heading: How the model generated code
items: **Bottom-up by layer.** Foundation, record, domain, surface, compose, app. After each change lower down, the type checker's error list became the work list.

**Wide, guarded edits.** Not one interactive edit in the main thread. Each of 170 scripted replacements asserted a single match, alongside 70 whole-file writes. Fast across many files, and loud when the code was not as expected.
**Gates as context.** It planned from 17 gate files, not 285 sources. One exported function per file kept units small: a median of 10 lines.
**A check for every 1.5 writes.** Type checks, test runs, topology checks, production builds and 30 screenshot runs, interleaved with building.
**Text in parallel, code in one thread.** Sub-agents wrote the specification and 1,029 lines of bilingual content. Parallel text drifted in numbers, names and privacy, and needed harmonising.
**Decisions written as built.** ADRs followed verified code and record what testing found. The owner saw most of them only afterwards.
**Defects at the boundaries, not in the logic:** framework serialisation, the CSS cascade, Ukrainian inflection, scenario continuity, the meaning of a parameter.
**Amplification.** A 472-character directive became 263 changed files. Acceptance rested on evidence (screenshots, check output, evaluations), not on reading diffs.

ownWords.heading: In the model's own words
quotes: I am fastest where rules are mechanical: types, topology, gates. I am slowest where meaning is involved: what a number says to a donor, or what a label reveals about a village.
The browser taught me more than my tests. With everything green, walking each role still found 13 defects.
Two flaws were my own designs: settings that became ‘custom’ when saved unchanged, and a demo that could not be walked. Using the product found them; reading the code did not.
The vaults are my memory. After my context was compacted mid-iteration, I carried on from files, not from recollection.
I reviewed my own work. That is the weakest link: a fresh reviewer would see what I cannot.
Construction took 16% of the elapsed time. The owner's attention set the pace, so easy acceptance matters more than faster building.

nextTime.heading: Next time
items: Restate each directive before building: goal, scope, evidence.
Commit by layer, citing the ADR and the iteration.
Run the walk, the crawl and the screenshots in CI.
Add an independent review before acceptance.
